input.description: Write one structured JSON object or a rows array into a workspace table. The destination is either table_ref (an existing Catalog table selected for each run) or table_name together with a required database_ref Catalog database picker object; a table_name without database_ref is invalid. For auto-create or same-name reuse, select the parent database with database_ref and keep table_name as literal text; json_schema continues to drive auto-creation. The two destination modes are mutually exclusive. Exactly one payload group is required: raw_json and/or values, or a non-empty rows array. Unknown fields are rejected.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Optional column mapping. Each key is a destination column name; each value is a payload key, or an array of payload keys tried in order, whose first non-empty value fills that column when the payload has no non-empty value under the column name itself. Example: {"ticket_created_at": "created_at"} writes the payload created_at value into column ticket_created_at. Entries whose key is not a destination column are ignored. A mapped payload key is not reported as unmatched, but when it also names a destination column its value is still written to that column.

fields.name: column_whitelist
fields.description: Explicit subset-write mode. Only listed columns are written and other payload keys are intentionally ignored. When omitted, every payload key must match a table column or an aliases mapping.

fields.name: database_ref
fields.description: Catalog database picker value for table_name mode. Bind the complete picker object; database_id is the authoritative identity resolved by the worker at runtime.

fields.name: catalog_id
fields.description: Catalog numeric ID when supplied by the picker.

fields.name: database_id
fields.description: Selected Catalog database numeric ID.

fields.name: database_name
fields.description: Selected database display or physical name when supplied by the picker; runtime resolution still uses database_id.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Catalog picker resource kind.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Selected database display name when supplied by the picker.

fields.name: json_schema
fields.description: JSON Schema describing the expected row structure. When the table does not exist, this schema drives auto-creation. When the table already exists, every schema property missing from that table is added as a new column before the write. Each property becomes a column with type inferred from the schema type (string→TEXT, integer→BIGINT, number→DOUBLE, boolean→BOOLEAN, array/object→JSON). Property names must be valid MatrixOne column names; invalid names fail explicitly. An auto-created table always adds id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY and created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; schema properties or payload keys named id or created_at do not create columns of their own. A payload created_at value is written into that TIMESTAMP column, which accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS and rejects a trailing Z or UTC offset; keep source timestamps under another field name to store them as text.

fields.name: policy
fields.description: Conflict policy for an existing target row handled by this call. Omitted input uses OVERWRITE; this setting does not coordinate concurrent calls.

fields.name: raw_json
fields.description: One non-empty JSON object, supplied either as an object value or a string that decodes to a JSON object. Arrays, scalar JSON values, malformed strings, empty objects, and empty strings fail when passed directly. A rows array may feed raw_json only through an explicit jq transform that selects or reshapes it into exactly one non-empty object; a direct rows-array binding remains invalid. The worker does not repair truncated or fenced JSON. Without column_whitelist, every decoded key must match an existing destination column or be explicitly mapped by aliases. raw_json may be combined with values; it is mutually exclusive with rows.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Structured row objects to insert or upsert atomically in this call. Input field names must match destination columns after aliases or column_whitelist are applied. Every row is validated against the destination columns before the transaction starts; rows is mutually exclusive with raw_json and values. This does not serialize or deduplicate other calls targeting the same destination.

fields.name: table_name
fields.description: Literal physical destination table name alternative to table_ref. For newly authored workflows, pair it with database_ref selected through the Catalog database picker. Keep table_name as text. If the named table exists it is reused; otherwise json_schema or raw data drives auto-creation. Use table_ref instead when selecting an existing MOI table.

fields.name: table_ref
fields.description: Existing Catalog destination table selected separately for each workflow run. Declare this as a workflow-run input when the workflow accepts an existing MOI table without fixing its identity during design. The selected table must contain every incoming field after aliases or column_whitelist are applied. The worker resolves database and table names from table_id; table_ref is mutually exclusive with table_name and every database selector.

input.description: Write one structured JSON object or a rows array into a workspace table. The mutated resource is identified by table_ref, or by table_name together with a Catalog database_ref picker object. Select an existing Catalog destination separately for each workflow run with table_ref. For auto-create or same-name reuse, select the parent database with database_ref and keep table_name as literal text; json_schema continues to drive auto-creation. database/database_id and omission of every database selector remain compatibility-only paths for already persisted workflows and are not the authoring path. The two destination modes are mutually exclusive. Exactly one payload group is required: raw_json and/or values, or a non-empty rows array. Unknown fields are rejected.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Optional column mapping. Each key is a destination column name; each value is a payload key, or an array of payload keys tried in order, whose first non-empty value fills that column when the payload has no non-empty value under the column name itself. Example: {"ticket_created_at": "created_at"} writes the payload created_at value into column ticket_created_at. Entries whose key is not a destination column are ignored. A mapped payload key is not reported as unmatched, but when it also names a destination column its value is still written to that column.

fields.name: column_whitelist
fields.description: Explicit subset-write mode. Only listed columns are written and other payload keys are intentionally ignored. When omitted, every payload key must match a table column or an aliases mapping.

fields.name: database
fields.description: Compatibility-only physical database name used with table_name by already persisted workflows. New workflows must use the database_ref Catalog picker; this field is intentionally absent from input_ui_schema.

fields.name: database_id
fields.description: Compatibility-only database numeric ID used with table_name by already persisted workflows. New workflows must bind the complete database_ref Catalog picker object; this scalar is intentionally absent from input_ui_schema.

fields.name: json_schema
fields.description: JSON Schema describing the expected row structure. When the table does not exist, this schema drives auto-creation. When the table already exists, every schema property missing from that table is added as a new column before the write. Each property becomes a column with type inferred from the schema type (string→TEXT, integer→BIGINT, number→DOUBLE, boolean→BOOLEAN, array/object→JSON). Property names must be valid MatrixOne column names; invalid names fail explicitly. An auto-created table always adds id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY and created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; schema properties or payload keys named id or created_at do not create columns of their own. A payload created_at value is written into that TIMESTAMP column, which accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS and rejects a trailing Z or UTC offset; keep source timestamps under another field name to store them as text.

fields.name: policy
fields.description: Conflict policy for an existing target row handled by this call. Omitted input uses OVERWRITE; this setting does not coordinate concurrent calls.

fields.name: raw_json
fields.description: One non-empty JSON object, supplied either as an object value or a string that decodes to a JSON object. Arrays, scalar JSON values, malformed strings, empty objects, and empty strings fail when passed directly. A rows array may feed raw_json only through an explicit jq transform that selects or reshapes it into exactly one non-empty object; a direct rows-array binding remains invalid. The worker does not repair truncated or fenced JSON. Without column_whitelist, every decoded key must match an existing destination column or be explicitly mapped by aliases. raw_json may be combined with values; it is mutually exclusive with rows.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Structured row objects to insert or upsert atomically in this call. Input field names must match destination columns after aliases or column_whitelist are applied. Every row is validated against the destination columns before the transaction starts; rows is mutually exclusive with raw_json and values. This does not serialize or deduplicate other calls targeting the same destination.

fields.name: table_name
fields.description: Literal physical destination table name alternative to table_ref. For newly authored workflows, pair it with database_ref selected through the Catalog database picker. Keep table_name as text. If the named table exists it is reused; otherwise json_schema or raw data drives auto-creation. Use table_ref instead when selecting an existing MOI table.

fields.name: table_ref

Declare this as a workflow-run input when the workflow accepts an existing MOI table without fixing its identity during design. The selected table must contain every incoming field after aliases or column_whitelist are applied. The worker resolves database and table names from table_id; table_ref is mutually exclusive with table_name and every database selector.

input.description: Send one HTTP request to an external API, webhook, or HTTP endpoint. Use this as the user-facing API node instead of catalog:http.request.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Optional JSON request body. Missing or null means no request body. Objects and arrays are sent as JSON text.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: Optional request headers object. Missing or null means no extra request headers. Every value must be a string, for example {"Authorization":"Bearer token"}.

fields.name: idempotency_key_mode
fields.description: Optional idempotency header policy. Empty or omitted leaves headers unchanged; workflow_execution_id sets Idempotency-Key from the current workflow execution and forbids an explicit Idempotency-Key header.

fields.name: method
fields.description: HTTP method. Must be one of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD.

fields.name: timeout_seconds
fields.description: Optional request timeout in seconds. Missing, null, or 0 uses the node default timeout.

fields.name: url
fields.description: Absolute HTTP or HTTPS request URL.

output.description: HTTP response envelope returned by the API node. HTTP 4xx/5xx responses are represented by status_code and body; transport failures return a node error.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Raw HTTP response body.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: HTTP response headers object. Each key is a response header name and each value is the header string reported by Go's http client.

fields.name: json
fields.description: Parsed JSON value when body is valid JSON; otherwise null.

fields.name: status_code
fields.description: HTTP response status code.
